\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انتخاب} (intikhāb)}{انتخاب (intikhāb)}]{\ar{انتخاب} (intikhāb) — an election}

\label{lesson:AR-C378-intikhab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a parliament, then the Arabic for a constitution.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انتخاب}}
\textbf{\ar{انتخاب}} — \emph{intikhāb} — \textquotedblleft{}an election\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{شارك} \ar{الناس} \ar{في} \ar{الانتخاب} \ar{بأعداد} \ar{كبيرة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{shāraka an-nās fī al-intikhāb bi-aʿdād kabīra.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People took part in the election in large numbers.
\end{quote}

More often plural: \ar{الانتخابات}, \emph{al-intikhābāt}, the elections.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انتخاب}} (\emph{intikhāb}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-kh-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to choose, to select\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Intikhāb} is the Form VIII verbal noun, a choosing out: an election.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intikhāb}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{intikhāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{shāraka an-nās fī al-intikhāb bi-aʿdād kabīra.} — People took part in the election in large numbers.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for a parliament, then the Arabic for a constitution, then say \emph{intikhāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{انتخاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}An election\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{انتخب} (intakhaba)}{انتخب (intakhaba)}]{\ar{انتخب} (intakhaba) — to elect}

\label{lesson:AR-C378-intakhaba}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for a constitution, then the Arabic for an election.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{انتخب}}
\textbf{\ar{انتخب}} — \emph{intakhaba} — \textquotedblleft{}to elect\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{انتخب} \ar{السكان} \ar{امرأة} \ar{شابة}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{intakhaba as-sukkān imraʾa shābba.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The residents elected a young woman.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{ينتخب}, \emph{yantakhib}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{انتخب}} (\emph{intakhaba}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-kh-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to choose, to select\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form VIII, to choose out for oneself: to elect.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{صوت} (ṣawwata)}{صوت (ṣawwata)}]{\ar{صوت} (ṣawwata) — to vote}

\label{lesson:AR-C378-sawwata}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for an election, then the Arabic for to elect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{صوت}}
\textbf{\ar{صوت}} — \emph{ṣawwata} — \textquotedblleft{}to vote\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{صوتت} \ar{أمي} \ar{في} \ar{الصباح} \ar{الباكر}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ṣawwatat ummī fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ al-bākir.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My mother voted early in the morning.
\end{quote}

Present: \ar{يصوت}, \emph{yuṣawwit}.

\ar{صوت} \ar{لـ}, voted for. The noun \ar{صوت}, \emph{ṣawt}, voice, also means a vote.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{صوت}} (\emph{ṣawwata}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{ṣ-w-t}, \textquotedblleft{}to make a sound\textquotedblright{} (Lane). It is Form II, to raise one's voice: to cast a vote.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣawwata}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣawwata}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ṣawwatat ummī fī aṣ-ṣabāḥ al-bākir.} — My mother voted early in the morning.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for an election, then the Arabic for to elect, then say \emph{ṣawwata} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ar{صوت} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To vote\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{ناخب} (nākhib)}{ناخب (nākhib)}]{\ar{ناخب} (nākhib) — a voter}

\label{lesson:AR-C378-nakhib}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to elect, then the Arabic for to vote.

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{ناخب}}
\textbf{\ar{ناخب}} — \emph{nākhib} — \textquotedblleft{}a voter\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{ذهب} \ar{كل} \ar{ناخب} \ar{إلى} \ar{مدرسة} \ar{القرية}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dhahaba kullu nākhib ilā madrasat al-qarya.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Every voter went to the village school.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{ناخب}} (\emph{nākhib}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{n-kh-b}, \textquotedblleft{}to choose, to select\textquotedblright{} (Lane). \emph{Nākhib} is the active participle, one who chooses: a voter.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ar{مرشح} (murashshaḥ)}{مرشح (murashshaḥ)}]{\ar{مرشح} (murashshaḥ) — a candidate}

\label{lesson:AR-C378-murashshah}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Arabic for to vote, then the Arabic for a voter.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ar{مرشح}}
\textbf{\ar{مرشح}} — \emph{murashshaḥ} — \textquotedblleft{}a candidate\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ar{تكلم} \ar{المرشح} \ar{عن} \ar{خطته}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{takallama al-murashshaḥ ʿan khiṭṭatih.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The candidate talked about his plan.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ar{مرشح}} (\emph{murashshaḥ}) is built on the native Arabic root \emph{r-sh-ḥ}, \textquotedblleft{}to sweat, to ooze\textquotedblright{} (Lane). Lane gives Form II for a mother training her young; \emph{murashshaḥ} is one made ready for a post: a candidate.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for giving reasons and opinions.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{murashshaḥ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{takallama al-murashshaḥ ʿan khiṭṭatih.} — The candidate talked about his plan.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Arabic for to vote, then the Arabic for a voter, then say \emph{murashshaḥ} again
\end{itemize}
